title: Supreme Court: Anti-Suit Injunction Against a UK Divorce Cannot Rest on Mere Apprehension of an Unenforceable Decree
case_name: Mihir Prakash Bajoria v. Vidushi Jain Bajoria
card_summary: The couple married in Kolkata in 2018 and settled in London. When the wife filed for divorce there, the husband got an anti-suit injunction from an Alipore court, arguing a UK decree on irretrievable breakdown would not bind him under the Hindu Marriage Act. The Supreme Court upheld Calcutta HC's order vacating that injunction, holding it cannot rest on mere apprehension a foreign decree may prove unenforceable.
card_tip: Do not seek an anti-suit injunction against a spouse's foreign divorce just because the foreign ground is unavailable under the HMA; show real oppression or vexation, not just an enforceability risk.
verification_notes: The 2018 Kolkata marriage, the London residence, the Alipore injunction, the Calcutta High Court's vacating order, the 22 September 2026 Supreme Court decision (2026 INSC 1034) and the bench of Justices Bhatti and Anjaria are corroborated across LiveLaw, LawChakra and SupremeToday.ai reports of the same judgment.
